classification.difficultyReason: Translate two resource limits into inequalities, find their boundary intersection, identify the common first-quadrant region, and test a production plan against both limits.

content.prompt: A manufacturer produces two types of chairs: wooden ($x$) and metal ($y$). Each wooden chair requires 3 hours of carpentry and 1 hour of painting. Each metal chair requires 2 hours of carpentry and 2 hours of painting. The factory has at most 60 hours available for carpentry and 40 hours for painting each week.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch the feasible region for the production of chairs.

answer.short:
$x\geq0$, $y\geq0$, $3x+2y\leq60$ and $x+2y\leq40$. The closed feasible region has vertices $(0,0)$, $(20,0)$, $(10,15)$ and $(0,20)$.

Shade below both resource boundaries in the first quadrant. Actual chair quantities have integer coordinates.
answer.worked:
The resource constraints and non-negative quantities give
$$\begin{align*}3x+2y&\leq60&&\text{(carpentry)}\\x+2y&\leq40&&\text{(painting)}\\x&\geq0\\y&\geq0.\end{align*}$$
The boundary lines meet at
$$\begin{align*}(3x+2y)-(x+2y)&=60-40\\2x&=20\\x&=10\\10+2y&=40\\2y&=30\\y&=15.\end{align*}$$
Draw solid boundary lines. Shade the common region below both lines in the first quadrant, including the boundaries. Its vertices are $(0,0)$, $(20,0)$, $(10,15)$ and $(0,20)$. Only integer-coordinate points represent actual chair-production choices.

spec.sourceRegion: Problem 2(a); answer book PDF page 34, P2(a)
spec.description: Corrected first-quadrant feasible region. The source graph has no grid or numeric axis ticks. Blue and red distinguish the resource boundaries; light blue identifies their common feasible region.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Is it possible to make 15 wooden chairs and 20 metal chairs in one week? Justify your response.

answer.short: No. Carpentry requires 85 hours and painting requires 55 hours, exceeding the limits of 60 and 40 hours respectively.
answer.worked:
For $x=15$ and $y=20$:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Carpentry hours}&=3(15)+2(20)\\\text{Carpentry hours}&=85>60\\\text{Painting hours}&=15+2(20)\\\text{Painting hours}&=55>40.\end{align*}$$
Both resource limits are exceeded, so the production plan is not feasible.
